 24m ago 10.03 EST Aaron Bower was at Elland Road. Here’s his report. Thanks for reading this MBM.
 Okafor’s Leeds winner adds insult to Tel’s injury for Tottenham as Bogle escapes red Read more Share 25m ago 10.02 EST De Zerbi has 'big confidence' in referee
 Roberto De Zerbi – who having picked up a booking today will be missing from the touchline for the visit of Ipswich in a fortnight’s time - talks to TNT. “The first half, we played well … the second half, we deserved to lose the game … we lost all duels … we didn’t play like we can … it’s a journey for us … we can learn from this game … there was a way to play better … to defend better … I am sorry for the result but most of all I am sorry for the performance in the second half … we didn’t play like a top team … we played without the right spirit, the right character, the right physicality in the duels … it is tough to accept this defeat after those good games in a row … but it is part of the journey … the most important thing is to understand why we didn’t play well in the second half … it’s just a mental aspect.”
 As for the Bogle tackle: “Pedro Porro was [booked for] a normal duel … an incredible yellow card … the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see so I can’t say … I have big confidence in the referee … nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not … there was the VAR … if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know … we have to keep our eyes on the performance, which can improve.”
 He also reports that James Maddison was not fit enough to play much more than 15 minutes, hence his remaining on the bench.
 Share 35m ago 09.53 EST Farke: Bogle is 'my butterfly'
 Daniel Farke speaks to TNT Sports. “We are very happy against an in-form Tottenham side … the second half it was never in doubt … we missed a few chances but we were relentless … great commitment … great unity … fully deserved … Noah Okafor was a week out … so credit to the doctors … they told me to stay disciplined and only put him on the pitch for 15, 20 minutes … an ice-cold finish … we need to stay cool in the head … close the centre … be technically spot on … to be brave … committed in the moments when we can press … I think we found a good balance today … it’s good to have the winning feeling back in the dressing room, so credit to my boys.”
 His view on the Bogle tackle: “I haven’t watched it back … there were several doubtful situations … a possible handball … I just know Jayden Bogle does nothing with any bad intention … it looked like a coming together … an unlucky outcome that Mathys [Tel] is injured … we wish him all the best … the last thing Bogle is, is a nasty player … he is probably the softest player in the whole league … I always call him my butterfly! … never he has bad intention, which I can guarantee, but of course I hope Mathys can recover quickly.”
 Share 45m ago 09.43 EST Post-match postbag. “Thankfully, on NBC in the US, the Nevilles were on at halftime to explain that the Bogle tackle looks worse than it actually was, and that as fullbacks, they did that a thousand times in their career. Case closed!” – Robert Bodendorf
 “The absurdity of the English ref clown show is making the Premier League unwatchable. They are far too concerned with narrative and managing the game rather than officiating it. You need no other evidence beyond them looking at a clear and obvious red card for five minutes with their hands over their heads as they agonise over giving Spurs a third match against ten men while Leeds need a win. It’s a joke and it’s going to kill off the ‘best league in the world’ status the Prem has right now” – Travis Antolik
 “Not a penalty. The reverse angle shows it hits the shoulder, not a hand ball. Red card all day” – Conor Clarke
 Share 49m ago 09.38 EST Noah Okafor speaks to TNT. “All I want is to help the team as much as I can … happy about the goal but more happy with the three points.” And here’s how those points change everything, ahead of what remains of matchday 10, with Spurs remaining in tenth spot and Leeds leapfrogging them into eighth.

 Share 53m ago 09.35 EST Leeds celebrate their big win as local lads Kaiser Chiefs predict a riot. They were much the better side in the second half, the only surprise being the deciding goal took so long to arrive. Its scorer Noah Okafor wasn’t hanging around, mind: he’d only been on the pitch for 97 seconds when he found the net! On the balance of play, it’s a richly deserved victory for Leeds, who might have had a penalty early doors – conflicting pictorial evidence exists of the ball hitting Mateus Fernandes on the arm/shoulder, so pick your poison and take your position – then completely dominated the second half. The one huge elephant in the room, however, is Jayden Bogle’s crude connection with Mathys Tel’s achilles, which should have resulted in a first-half red card, and would surely have changed the course of the game. But here we are. Premier League football, at its wild and unpredictable best, for all its faults.
 View image in fullscreen Deep joy for Tarik Muharemovic and James Trafford at the final whistle! Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.40 EST 1h ago 09.28 EST FULL TIME: Leeds United 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur
 The whistle goes, and Leeds claim three well-earned points. Much the better side. Bogle on Tel, though.
 Share 1h ago 09.27 EST 90 min +4: Williams-Barnett crosses from the left. Gray flicks on for Bentancur, free on the right-hand corner of the six-yard box! But Bentancur can’t control, and Trafford claims. Turns out Bentancur was clearly offside anyway. But Leeds hearts were in mouths for a hot second there.
 Share 1h ago 09.25 EST 90 min +3: Longstaff and Bogle – the latter very fortunate to still be around, at the risk of belabouring that particular point – are replaced by Rodon and Gruev.
 Share 1h ago 09.24 EST 90 min +2: Tonali dribbles down the left and finds Williams-Barnett in the box with a low cross. Williams-Barnett tries to sort his feet out for a shot, but can’t manage it. Leeds clear again.
 Share 1h ago 09.23 EST 90 min +1: Robertson swings a free kick in from the left. Van Hecke rises highest, and guides a header towards the top right. Trafford extends fully and tips around the post. The resulting corner leads to a throw, which is flung in illegally by Kulusevski. Pressure off!
 View image in fullscreen James Trafford saves the day for Leeds! Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Share Updated at  09.28 EST 1h ago 09.22 EST 90 min: There will be four additional minutes.
 Share 1h ago 09.21 EST 89 min: Wilson steps across Tonali, who swings an arm to bring him down and picks up a booking.
 Share 1h ago 09.20 EST 88 min: Meanwhile, Leeds are doing a marvellous job of containing Spurs, who are trying to respond, but can’t get anywhere near their opponents’ box. Leeds’ xG is now exactly 2 to Tottenham’s 0.28.
 Share 1h ago 09.19 EST 87 min: No, is the answer to that. Not a single one.
 Share 1h ago 09.18 EST 86 min: TNT are interviewing Nmecha as the game goes on, a box popping up and invading the action. Did any football fan ask for this sort of thing?
 Share 1h ago 09.16 EST 84 min: Kudus makes way for the 18-year-old Williams-Barnett. When the game restarts, Calvert-Lewin once again tears clear down the right, but doesn’t back himself to shoot, turning around instead and laying off to Okafor. The move breaks down. That’s a couple of big chances butchered by Calvert-Lewin today.
 Share 1h ago 09.14 EST 82 min: Spurs haven’t won any of their last 49 matches in which they’ve gone behind. No wonder Roberto De Zerbi looks thoroughly miserable. That goal was no more than Leeds deserved; they’ve been by far the better team in this second half.
 Share 1h ago 09.13 EST 80 min: VAR has a look at a possible handball by Wilson, but there was no touch with his arm. The goal stands!
 Share 1h ago 09.12 EST GOAL! Leeds United 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Okafor 79)
 Bard throws in from the left. Wilson swivels just inside the box, chesting down and teeing up Okafor, who takes a touch infield before lashing a shot across Kinsky and into the bottom left! Lovely move, and what a substitution!
 View image in fullscreen Substitute Noah Okafor breaks the deadlock! Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters Share Updated at  09.22 EST 1h ago 09.10 EST 77 min: Kinsky annoys Longstaff again by pawing his corner clear. Then Leeds make a double change, sending on Wilson and Okafor for Tanaka and Nmecha.
 Share 1h ago 09.09 EST 76 min: … but Spurs don’t clear their lines particularly well, and Tanaka strides down the left to win another Leeds corner. Longstaff, who must be wondering how he didn’t score, to take.
 Share 1h ago 09.08 EST 75 min: Bogle advances down the right and crosses low for Longstaff, who turns and launches a rising shot goalwards from 12 yards. It’s a superb effort, and heading in, but met by the fingertips of Kinsky. What a save! The ball clears the bar, and nothing comes of the corner.
 Share 1h ago 09.05 EST 73 min: Kulusevski and Bentancur combine down the right, but at such slow speed that Leeds close down all avenues to their box. Spurs have not created very much this afternoon.
 Share 1h ago 09.03 EST 71 min: From the set piece, Bogle shoots. The ball hits Bentancur. Leeds claim a penalty, but that’s hit Bentancur on the chest. No sir!
 Share 1h ago 09.02 EST 70 min: Bard loops down the middle. Nmecha tries to loop over Kinsky, who tips onto the bar. But he was offside. Then Calvert-Lewin fails to hit the target. But Kinsky takes his sweet time over the restart, so the referee awards a corner to Leeds!
 Share 1h ago 09.01 EST 68 min: Spurs play some possession stuff. They don’t really go anywhere for a while, but suddenly spring into action, Gallagher bringing the ball down on the edge of the Leeds D before pearling a low drive inches wide of the bottom left. Not entirely sure Trafford was getting to that. Spurs fans thought that was in, so are jeered for their cheer not long after.
 Share 1h ago 08.58 EST 66 min: … so Spurs make a triple change, replacing the ineffective Marmoush and Fernandes, plus Porro, who is on one-and-a-half yellows, with Kulusevski, Bentancur and Gallagher. Gray will take over from Porro at right-back.
 Share 2h ago 08.57 EST 64 min: Leeds have had seven attempts on goal during this second half. Spurs are yet to generate a single one.
 Share 2h ago 08.55 EST 63 min: Calvert-Lewin, Bard and Longstaff combine well down the left. The ball’s rolled infield for Ampadu, who shoots from 25 yards. The ball takes a huge deflection to the left, and had it stayed on target, it was a goal, because Kinsky had committed to diving the other way. But it squeaks out for a corner, which Kinsky claims. Leeds are getting closer and closer.
 Share 2h ago 08.54 EST 62 min: Van de Ven again over-eggs his dribble out from the back. This time he loses the ball, allowing Nmecha to enter the box from the left and aim a curler towards the top right. It’s not a good effort, and easily blocked.
 Share 2h ago 08.53 EST 61 min: Leeds are romping ahead in the xG stakes. It’s 1.11 to 0.22.
 Share 2h ago 08.52 EST 60 min: Porro clips Bard, who was advancing down the left, from behind. It should be a yellow. It’s not, though, presumably because it would have been a second yellow for Porro, and you know how referees process that sort of situation. Porro is now in the last-chance saloon. Meanwhile nothing comes of the resulting free kick.
 Share 2h ago 08.50 EST 58 min: The pace doesn’t drop, but passes are no longer sticking. All a bit messy for now.
 Share 2h ago 08.48 EST 56 min: Van de Ven over-elaborates when dribbling out from the back, and is nearly stripped by Longstaff. Had the Leeds man completed the challenge, he was through on goal. Van de Ven breathes out.
 Share 2h ago 08.47 EST 55 min: Tonali, dropping deep, tries to release Kudus down the right but has to settle for a corner. Kudus ambles across to take it. He exchanges passes with Solanke, then Robertson finally crosses long. Leeds deal with it. A bit of a waste.
 Share 2h ago 08.46 EST 53 min: Calvert-Lewin romps into space down the inside-right channel, chasing a fine Longstaff pass. He should shoot upon reaching the area, but lays off to Tanaka instead, who leans back and skies over the bar. Huge chance spurned.
 Share 2h ago 08.45 EST 52 min: Porro slides in, over the ball, and catches Nmecha on the shin. It’s a yellow. It should be a yellow. But Bogle’s far worse action in the first half should have been that at the very least . Roberto De Zerbi highlights this inherent contradiction, and is also booked for his trouble. Consistency? Good luck in your search for that.
 Share 2h ago 08.42 EST 50 min: Bogle crosses from the right. Calvert-Lewin prepares to sidefoot home from six yards, only for Van de Ven to nip in ahead of him, and slice the ball over his own bar and wide left. Then from the corner, hit long by Longstaff, Calvert-Lewin heads goalwards. Solanke blocks on his own line, then Elvedi heads wide left from close range. It should be 1-0.
 View image in fullscreen Close for Leeds! Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock Share Updated at  08.58 EST 2h ago 08.40 EST 48 min: Ampadu throws long from the right. Van de Ven clears. Leeds have had no joy with their long-throw weapon so far.
 Share 2h ago 08.38 EST 46 min: Bard’s very first act is to whip in a glorious low cross from his position on the left. Calvert-Lewin is on his heels and can’t connect. That was begging to be rammed home.
 Share 2h ago 08.37 EST Leeds get the second half started. They’ve replaced Gudmundsson with Bard.
 Share 2h ago 08.29 EST Half-time postbag. “Both feet are off the ground. That’s Bogle’s entire weight on Tel’s Achilles. That can lead to a serious injury. Bizarre decision” – Martin Perring
 “Why do red cards exist if not precisely to protect players?” – John from Norway
 “The most insane thing about VAR, and there are so many insane things about it, is that we have to watch replays of a player OBVIOUSLY doing a red-card challenge one thousand times in slow-motion, and it ends with not even a yellow. The chicken-shit nature of it all, the incompetence, all elevated because of technology. I hate it so, so much” – Øivind Idsø
 “There’s overthinking it, as you say, but this is like they’ve been given a task to find a reason for not giving that as a red, rocking and rolling desperately, frame-by-frame. The explanation they release for not giving a red should be a corker. Meanwhile, whatever happened to ‘clear and obvious’? VAR is almost single-handedly turning me into a grumpy old man. I’ll be off out now to shout at some pigeons” – Rob Knap
 “I’ve supported VAR from the start. It was always going to have teething issues as it was implemented, and it was never going to 100% eliminate mistakes. Subjectivity is still a thing. But, my word, they don’t half make it hard to defend at times. It should be established now, a mature technology with most of the errors ironed out. If anything, though, It’s getting worse. I’m not in the ‘Bin it’ camp yet, but I’m a lot closer than I was at the start of the season” – Matt Dony
 “Committees are an extremely useful method for decision making, especially when people have time to deliberate. But perhaps football refereeing isn’t suited to committees” – Kári Tulinius
 “That would have been a red card at Elland Road in the 70s ” – Gary Naylor
 Share 2h ago 08.22 EST HALF TIME: Leeds United 0-0 Tottenham Hotspur
 Leeds should have had a penalty; they should also have had a man sent off. The players walk down the tunnel. The referee was planning to drive away in his car, but the doors and square wheels have fallen off and there’s all smoke coming out of the radiator.
 Share 2h ago 08.21 EST 45 min +5: Ampadu throws long from the left. Van Hecke powers a header miles clear. Ampadu has another go. Van Hecke batters clear again. The xG does not change.
 Share 2h ago 08.20 EST 45 min +4: The xG, for what that’s worth, is 0.19 to 0.22. Meanwhile Roberto De Zerbi continues to give the fourth official the what-for. His post-match interview could make for good entertainment.
 Share 2h ago 08.18 EST 45 min +2: Fernandes slices a low drive miles off target. After nearly boiling over, this half is now fizzling out, which is probably for the best all round.
 Share 2h ago 08.17 EST 45 min: There will be six minutes of additional first-half time, most of which a result of the on-field referee and VAR spending ages failing to make a decision.
 Share 2h ago 08.15 EST 44 min: Kudus fizzes a tempting low cross through the Leeds six-yard box from the right. What a ball. But neither Gray nor Solanke respond. Any touch and it was the opening goal.
 Share 2h ago 08.14 EST 43 min: Tel limps off. A heavy trudge, he’s in some difficulty. He’s replaced by Solanke.
 Share 2h ago 08.13 EST 42 min: Marmoush clips Muharemovic from behind. That should be a booking as well, but the referee has lost control of this with his unwillingness to make any sort of decision whatsoever. Meanwhile Tel goes down, he looks really unhappy.
 Share 2h ago 08.11 EST 40 min: Tel is getting dog’s abuse now. He’s also moving very gingerly, having recently had someone stand on his ankle.
 Share 2h ago 08.11 EST 39 min: Roberto De Zerbi isn’t happy about that. You can’t blame him. Meanwhile the game restarts, with Bogle, who shouldn’t be on the pitch, crossing for Nmencha, who plants a header straight at Kinsky. Had that gone in, there would have been some wild scenes all right.
 Share 2h ago 08.09 EST 38 min: No red card, no serious foul play. That is preposterous enough in itself; that there’s not even a yellow is beyond a joke. The on-field referee should have seen that, at the very least.
 Share 2h ago 08.07 EST 37 min: VAR is flapping taking a long time over this. You can overthink these things, you know.
 Share 2h ago 08.06 EST 36 min: It’s a really poor challenge, studs landing on Tel’s achilles, the Spurs player’s leg bending. It should be a red card.
 Share 2h ago 08.06 EST 35 min: VAR is in fact checking for a red card. The on-field referee, it should be noted, has completely abdicated responsibility.
 Share 2h ago 08.05 EST 34 min: Bogle leaves one on Tel, who was in the process of spinning him. It’s a really poor challenge, studs on ankle. A red card wouldn’t be out of the question here; there’s not even a yellow shown.
 View image in fullscreen Mathys Tel recieves treatment after the challenge from Jayden Bogle. Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Share Updated at  08.17 EST 2h ago 08.04 EST 33 min: A long pass down the left confuses Elvedi into conceding a corner with a misjudged backwards header. One corner leads to another, then Marmoush heads harmlessly wide. To be fair, Trafford has had next to nothing to do as well, if you ignore a couple of long-range shots scuffed straight at him.
